# Stone Lords · Book II, pp. 382–395
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	382
P	In the time of the <b>Makers</b> (page 264), the Stone Lords ruled the <b>Steplands</b> (page 372), the southern stretch of the <b>Huffel</b> <b>Peaks</b> (page 236), and the <b>South Manmarch</b> (page 350). They carved cities out of the hills. They raised towering monuments. They sang stone, crystal, and glass into impossible shapes.
P	The Stone Lords' empire was grand, but it was not all glory. It was built on the backs of countless human servants. And while the Stone Lords were not especially cruel, neither were they kind. They imposed order on their world, by whatever means necessary.
P	For, better than the other Makers, the Stone Lords knew the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412).
P	Knew the insidious songs that echoed in the deep. Knew the chaos promised. Knew that they must never, ever be freed.
P	And so, when the <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210) called on the Things Below to put down their own servants' rebellion, the Stone Lords turned on their brethren.
P	They shattered the Green Lords' lands and hunted down the survivors.
P	Yet: the seals had cracked. The Things Below sang all the louder. The Stone Lords themselves stood resolute, but their servants did not. Corruption seeped through their society like water finding cracks in a poorly laid foundation.
P	The end came swiftly. Sorcerers turned the city of Dulenn into a massive sinkhole, creating what is now <b>Blackwater Lake</b> (page 48). Seals were broken across the land and horrors slithered up through the tunnels. Mobs turned on their former masters.
P	One by one, the domains and cities of the Stone Lords fell into ruin.
P	The <b>Time of Cataclysm</b> (page 413) had arrived.
H2	Names
HR
P	Breton- and Cornish-inspired, but with extra vowels for a drawn-out sound:
P	Aenedellion, Caedour, Daenizel, Eelowain, Gaeille, Iaves, Kaeteal, Loiawen, Mearauwd, Neassa, Oaneaz, Paerrain, Rozainne, Saennaen, Taenguey, Wainoac, Yainniac
P	Combine with prefixes like "Aalz" ("the great"), "Skol" ("master"), or "Loaji" ("apprentice"), etc.

B	A petrified prisoner of the Stone Lords was recently reanimated, and must now make sense of this new age
B	While seeking shelter from the elements, the PCs stumble on a Stone Lord ruin
B	Hillfolk need help dealing with dangerous stone constructs that are running amok

P	1d12 theme
HR

P	2 Crystals/gems/<b>makerglass</b> (page 388): decorative, practical, or thrumming with power
P	3 Songs/resonance/vibrations/echoes:
P	to empower, shape, transform, or destroy
P	4 Seals/bindings/things trapped in stone: creatures/spirits/ideas/ memories/free will
P	5 Constructs/stone given life, or an approximation thereof
P	6 Authority/order/hierarchy/tradition

P	8 Bonds broken/seals opened/collapse and chaos/the Things Below set loose
P	9-12 Sized for giants, and roll 1d8 again

H3	Something trapped
P	For example:
B	Someone trapped in a stalagmite, their grasping hands, anguished face, and mournful moans just barely discernible
B	A hollow, seamless cube of rune-carved white stone, 6 feet per side, bitterly cold; a dozen <b>specters</b> (page 79) are sealed within, impotent and mad
B	A stretch of shining black flagstones, showing reflections of people long past; those who open their minds see a parade of memories, clear as day
B	A <b>construct</b> (page 392) with a crack in its "head," possessed by an evil spirit; bound in a circle of deeply-cut runes
B	A labyrinth of stone walls, the walkways forming a rune of binding, some sort of demon trapped in the center

H3	Strange geologies
P	For example:
B	A large grotto, unnaturally smooth and precise, like part of a sphere just vanished from the stone
B	A gorge cutting perpendicularly through a valley, the walls lined with glass
B	A tunnel or valley, shaped so that the smallest sounds echo echo echo
B	A cliff face, the striations perfectly smooth and parallel, the different strata strikingly different colors or types of stone
B	A slope entirely made of smooth, rounded stone; like an old lava flow, but chert, granite, or limestone
B	An enormous rock formation, shot through with dozens of small holes that catch the wind and sing a haunting melody.

H3	Monument, marker, or enigma
P	For example:
B	A crater of bare stone, 100 paces across, with a lozenge of black stone floating in the center, thrumming
B	A statue carved from a mountainside, fragments of its stone sword littering the valley below
B	A pedestal bearing two vast and trunkless legs of stone; hints of an inscription, now unreadable
B	Giant stone heads arrayed upon a slope, their faces faded yet still disapproving
B	A pylon of glass, 100 feet tall at least (and who knows how deeply set into the earth), faintly humming, faintly glowing
B	Great lines gouged into the earth, running for miles; meaningless from the surface, but making enormous runes when seen from on high
B	A large room in some cave or ruin, the charred bones of a giant at the center; bits of blackened bone/tooth/carapace litter the edge; hundreds of fist-sized shards of crystal are embedded in the walls
B	A chamber with dozens of glass cylinders, fixed vertically against a wall, each of differing length and width—some sort of instrument, perhaps?

Populate it with <b>lingering</b> <b>signs</b> (page 384), <b>artifacts</b> (page 388) and/or <b>dangers</b> of the Stone Lords (page 390) or the appropriate region.

HR
P	1 Dwelling (home, barracks, dormitory, prison, etc.)
P	2 Infrastructure (aqueduct, rampart, road, bridge, etc.)
P	3 Storage (vault, warehouse, library, museum, etc.)
P	4 Production (workshop, factory, mine, farm, etc.)
P	5 Esoteric (laboratory, experiment, power source, etc.)
P	6 Civic life (agora, theater, shrine, monument, tomb, etc.)
P	1d6 architectural elements
HR
P	1 Great slabs of marble/granite/limestone/etc., far too big for humans to lift
P	2 Seamless stone structures/tunnels, like they were poured or molded that way
P	3 Runes carved into stone and shaped out of walls, roads, tunnels, etc.
P	4 Crystals/makerglass: catching light/ wind, humming/glowing, chiming/ gonging
P	5 Stones/crystals that emanate emotion/mood/thoughts/memories
P	6 Grandiosity of scale, big enough to humble even the Makers Most Maker-ruins are sized for giants—people two or even three times as tall as humans—but often with smaller-scale rooms, passages, and so forth for their servants.
P	1d6 condition
HR
P	1-2 Shattered and laid waste by time, war, or vandalism; mostly buried, overgrown, collapsed; its purpose unrecognizable
P	3-4 Crumbling, largely buried, overgrown, or hidden away
P	5 Buried, overgrown, or hidden, but mostly intact
P	6 Fully visible and strangely well-preserved Many Stone Lord ruins were <b>reclaimed</b> (page 36) by the Barrow Builders at some point. See <b>Blackwater Lake</b> (page 51) and <b>Three Coven Lake</b> (page 442).

H3	A chalky potion
P	<i>magical</i>, <i>fragile</i>, <i>slow</i>
P	1d4 glass vials containing thick, gritty, whitish fluid. The stopper bears a mark of transformation, flesh, and stone.
P	When you <b><i>drink the whole potion while</i></b> <b><i>touching stone</i></b>, you transform (over a matter of minutes) into a mass of stone, similar to that which you touch. You retain awareness of your surroundings, blind but with excellent hearing.
PAGE	389
P	When you <b><i>attempt to end your lithic vigil</i></b>, roll +CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, you return to your original form, rested and invigorated—regain all your HP and clear all your debilities; <b>on a 7-9</b>, the transformation back is slow and arduous, mark a debility; <b>on a 6-</b>, you are stuck until someone pours another dose of the potion over you or communes with your spirit and helps you try again.

H3	Power-crystal
P	◇, <i>magical</i>, <i>dangerous</i>
P	A chunk of crystal the size of a clenched fist. If charged, it thrums or crackles with power. If depleted, it fills you with a sense of emptiness and longing.
P	When you <b><i>brandish the depleted power-crystal at a source of elemental energy</i></b>, roll
P	+CON: <b>on a 10+</b>, the crystal absorbs the energy fully and as safely as possible (it is now charged); <b>on a 7-9</b>, the crystal absorbs the energy (it's now charged) but pick 1:
B	You are harmed by the coursing energy, taking damage as the GM sees fit
B	The power stored in the crystal is extremely unstable, likely to discharge without warning
B	The crystal cracks; henceforth, treat a 10+ on this move as a 7-9, and you can't pick this option again.
P	In the hands of a skilled arcanist, a charged power-crystal can fuel or empower a magical effect (though this is dangerous). In the hands of the incautious, the reckless, or the desperate, it can split or crack, leading to a violent explosion.

H3	A scarred slab of marble
P	<i>immobile</i>, <i>magical</i>
P	A slab of once-beautiful stone, some 30 feet tall and about half again as wide, standing in a vaulted chamber, surrounded by deeply etched runes that speak of union and protection, consumption and sacrifice.
P	The stone bears a multitude of chips, gouges, and cracks. Dust and debris surround it.
P	When you <b><i>pry a chip of stone from the mar-</i></b>
P	<b><i>ble and swallow it whole, while standing</i></b>
P	<b><i>within the ring of runes</i></b>, your flesh becomes like stone and your DEX becomes -2 until the effect ends. The next three times you would suffer physical harm, the marble slab suffers the harm instead. The effect ends after the third blow.

H2	Dangers
HR
H3	Bound Entities
B	<b>Spirits of the wild</b> (page 356), especially elementals associated with earth, stone, and terrain, yoked by runecraft to serve the Stone Lord's needs
B	Spirits and beasts corrupted by <b>the</b> <b>Things Below</b> (page 412): petrified, encased in stone, or sealed away behind layers of runes
B	Would-be <b>sorcerer-kings</b> (page 34), petrified or otherwise imprisoned before they could cause too much trouble
B	<b>Ghosts</b> (page 76), mindlessly performing duties they were bound to perform in life, unaware that they could want anything else
B	<b>Primordial entities</b> (page 298), imprisoned by elaborate workings of crystal and rune, bound to serve or else locked away for safekeeping
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Unstable construction
P	The Stone Lords' work has stood for centuries, and they were the cleverest architects to ever walk this world. But the problem with grand, clever architecture is that when it fails, it fails spectacularly.
P	• A wall/floor/building is precariously perched, or a pillar/support/buttress supports an impossible load
P	• Something creaks/teeters/sways/groans
P	• Cracks form/debris tumbles/something starts to tip
P	• Age-old construction starts to fall like dominoes (run!)
P	• All is reduced to rubble, and dust, and death

H3	Construct
P	The Stone Lords were masters not only of shaping stone, but also of animating it and giving it the semblance of life.
P	Many such creations remain, though only a few still function and many of those function poorly.
P	Pick or roll a purpose, ability, size, power, sapience, and condition. Allow these elements to inform its physical form and construction.
P	1d12 purpose
HR
P	1-2 War/destruction/violence/coercion
P	3-4 Defense/protection/companionship
P	5-6 Experimentation/curiosity/practice
P	7-8 Construction/labor/convenience
P	9-10 Something obscure, or very specific
P	11-12 Roll 1d10 twice, combine
P	1d12 ability
HR
P	1 Nothing of note, just animated stone
P	2 Mental influence/control
P	3 Energy/elemental manipulation
P	4 Cunning/alertness/special senses
P	5 Disguise/camouflage/stealth
P	6 Restraints/snares/subdual
P	7 Ranged/area attack
P	8 Transformation/multipart form/ swarm
P	9 Prowess/mobility/speed
P	10 Destructive/vicious weaponry
P	11-12 Roll 1d10 twice Stone Lord constructs are typically blind but able to navigate by sound and sensing vibrations. Almost all are highly durable (+4 HP) and animated by more than biology (another +4 HP), with at least 3 Armor.
P	<b>1d12</b> size
HR
P	1 Cat-sized or smaller (<i>tiny</i>)
P	2-3 Like a human child (<i>small</i>)
P	4-7 Human-sized
P	8-10 Like a horse, a cart, etc. (<i>large</i>)
P	11-12 Like an elephant, or bigger (<i>huge</i>)
P	1d12 power
HR
P	1-3 Requires the presence of external source
P	4-8 Stores power, but must return "home" to recharge
P	9-11 Self-charging, but limited range/ activity
P	12 Self-powered/indefinite charge Power sources might include: singing crystals that broadcast energy; ingots of <b>aetherium</b> (page 404); veins of special stone transmitting power through floors; crystals that absorb telluric currents/vibrations; spirits bound in makerglass; etc.

HR

P	12 Person: fully sapient, potentially quite intelligent Ask yourself: where does this construct's sapience come from? Clever scripting?

H3	Lithic servant
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>implacable</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 11; <b>Armor</b> 3 (made of stone)
P	<b>Damage</b> stone fists d6 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> externally powered; bug-like intellect; blind; tremorsense <b>Instinct</b> to follow its last orders
P	• Act with eternal patience and endurance
P	• Act with no sense of consequence
P	• Hurt someone unintentionally while performing its tasks
P	Imagine one of those artists' mannequins, but full-sized and made of polished rock.
P	Two fingers and a thumb on each hand.
P	Faceless, expressionless, making a stone-on-stone grinding noise as they move.
P	They're most often found inert and covered in dust, waiting for some energy source—like a Stone Lord's song or a thrumming power-crystal—to give them "life." They'll then follow any orders given to them in the Stone Lord's tongue.
P	A few of these servants are still active, powered by inexhaustible sources in ancient halls. Their joints are worn smooth, their feet and hands ground down to nubs.
P	Some crawl on broken limbs, attempting to complete tasks that will never end.

HR
ICON	icons/construct.svg
H3	Stone sentinel
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>implacable</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 24; <b>Armor</b> 3 (made of stone)
P	<b>Damage</b> crushing fists d10+3 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>messy</i>, <i>forceful</i>, 3 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> can animate for only a few minutes at a time; dog-like mind; blind; tremorsense
P	<b>Instinct</b> to protect its ward
P	• Emit an ominous hum, a warning as it powers up
P	• Move with shocking, unexpected speed (but lose 1d4 HP)
P	• Erupt in flurry of violence (<i>area</i>, +2 damage, lose 2d4 HP)
P	Articulated statues, squat and wide, with huge stone hands, set to watch forever over some ruin, passage, or treasure. Their stone "minds" are full of vigilance, and violence.
P	Each sentinel bears a power-crystal in its chest, slowly absorbing vibrations through earth and stone. A few days of charging is enough to animate the construct for only a few minutes—which is usually more than enough time for it to repel (or crush) an invader.

H3	Mosaic swarm
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>amorphous</i>, <i>stealthy</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 24; <b>Armor</b> 3 (made of thousands of ceramic tiles)
P	<b>Damage</b> jagged fists of ceramic d10+3
P	(<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> externally powered; bug-like mind; blind; tremorsense; unharmed by piercing weapons; half damage from cutting weapons; vulnerable to attacks that are blunt and <i>forceful</i> or <i>area</i>
P	<b>Instinct</b> to destroy intruders
P	• Wait for intruders to get close, rattling softly
P	• Explode into a cloud of whirling ceramic tiles, d8+1 damage (<i>area</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	• Reform into a vaguely humanoid mass
P	Stone Lords adorned their halls with elaborate tilework and mosaics. Most of them were decorative. Most of them.
P	<b>Something interesting</b>: Either some spirit is possessing these tiles, or this is some sort of construct. If it's a spirit, there must be a tether. If it's a Stone Lord construct, well, the individual tiles are too small to power or direct themselves.
P	<b>Something useful</b>: The mosaic's frame remained on the wall, and it's glowing blue—aetherium runes! Destroy the runes, and the construct should fall apart.
ICON	icons/construct.svg
H3	Pacifier
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>small</i>, <i>construct</i>, <i>amorphous</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 4 (just a stone sphere)
P	<b>Damage</b> stupefying pulse of sound d6 (<i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>reload</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> must recharge after a few hours; limited autonomy; blind; tremorsense; has trouble with stairs; vulnerable to blunt, forceful attacks <b>Instinct</b> to keep mortals docile
P	• Sense and follow strong emotions
P	• Hum a soothing, pacifying sound (<i>near</i>, <i>area</i>)
P	• Sound the alarm, call for reinforcements
P	They're basically hollow stone spheres, maybe scratched and dinged but otherwise featureless. Often found in their little alcoves, charging. The Stone Lords would deploy them among the rowdier servants to keep things running smoothly.
P	When you <b><i>are in range of a pacifier's hum</i></b>, your emotions lose their edge. When you <b><i>rouse yourself to act violently</i></b>, urgently, or passionately, roll +WIS. If you <b><i>are in range</i></b> <b><i>of multiple pacifiers humming in unison</i></b>, you have disadvantage. <b>On a 10+</b>, you shake off the effect; <b>on a 7-9</b>, you shake off the effect but pick 1.
B	Your mind is addled; mark <i>dazed</i>
B	Your freedom is short-lived; the effect returns if you pause for any reason
B	You get carried away or take things too far, resulting in a consequence of the GM's choice
